name: K-Guard Entry
keyCorrections: If they step out of K-guard, your foot on the hip lost connection — re-establish the foot post immediately.
If they grab your head for a guillotine, your arm control is weak — swim your hand inside and pummel.
If you can't enter the leg entanglement, your angle under them is too shallow — scoot your hips closer.
description: Use K-guard to create an angle under the opponent's hips and enter backside or leg entanglement attacks with full control of their far leg.
shortInstruction: Foot on their far hip, hook their near leg, rotate under them — K-guard is the king of the modern leg attack system.
summary: K-guard is the most versatile entry point in modern no-gi leg locking. By placing one foot on the opponent's far hip and hooking their near leg with your other leg, you create a powerful angle under their center of mass. From here, you can attack the far leg (heel hook), take the back, or sweep to top position. K-guard is the glue that connects the bottom open guard to the leg entanglement system.
whyItWorks: The foot on their far hip controls their rotation and prevents them from stepping away.
The hook on their near leg gives you a lever to off-balance and enter leg entanglements.
Your body under their center of mass means you are always one movement away from sweeping or attacking.
Danaher principle: K-guard solves the problem of 'how to enter the legs without giving up position.'
commonMistakes: Letting the foot on their far hip slip down to their stomach — the foot must stay on the hip bone.
Not hooking their near leg deep enough — a shallow hook gives them the escape.
Keeping both feet on the mat — K-guard requires one foot elevated on their body at all times.
Going to K-guard without controlling their near arm — they will counter with a guillotine or kimura.
coachingCues: Foot on the hip, never the stomach.
Hook deep, control the arm, go under.
K-guard is the tunnel — the other side is the finish.
Feel their weight, move when they commit.
safetySummary: Keep your head off the mat when in K-guard — protect your neck from guillotine counters.
Control the near arm at all times — if they grab your head, you are in danger of a guillotine.
Do not extend for leg entries without controlling their far hip — they can kick free and counter with a kneebar.

systemLogic.corePrinciple: Seated guard: win the hand fight → place foot on far hip → hook near leg with other leg → rotate under their center → enter saddle, cross ashi, or back take.

decisionTree.action: They stand tall → enter cross ashi → heel hook.
They sit back → enter saddle → heel hook or back take.
They post a hand → sweep to top position.

moneyDetails: Your foot must be exactly on the hip bone (ASIS) — if it slides to the stomach or ribs, you lose control.
The near leg hook should be behind their thigh, not behind the knee — a deep hook gives you the angle.
Control their near arm by grabbing their sleeve, wrist, or triceps — this prevents them from counter-attacking.
Rotate your hips toward the ceiling as you enter K-guard — this opens the angle for leg entries.
nextStep: After K-guard entry, learn the K-guard matrix and the cross ashi heel hook system.
fixItFast: Foot slipping off the hip? Dig your heel into the hip bone — not the arch, the heel.
They grab your head? Pummel your hand inside their arm and reset the distance.
Can't rotate under them? Your hook is too shallow — scoot closer and re-hook deeper.
